sanskrit: taṃ visaṃjñaṃ mahārāja kirīṭibhayapīḍitam apovāha raṇāt sūto rakṣamāṇo dhanaṃjayāt
english: That senseless man, O great king, tormented by fear of the Diademed One, his charioteer bore away from the battle, guarding him from Dhanaṃjaya.

sanskrit: etasminn eva kāle tu vijayaḥ śatrutāpanaḥ nyavadhīt tāvakaṃ sainyaṃ śataśo 'tha sahasraśaḥ paśyatas tava putrasya tasya vīrasya bhārata
english: At that very moment, Vijaya, the scorcher of foes, slew your army by the hundreds and by the thousands, even as that heroic son of yours looked on, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: evam eṣa kṣayo vṛttas tāvakānāṃ paraiḥ saha krūro viśasano ghoro rājan durmantrite tava
english: Thus did this slaughter of your men come to pass against the foe — cruel, ruinous, and dreadful, O king, born of your evil counsel.

sanskrit: saṃśaptakāṃś ca kaunteyaḥ kurūṃś cāpi vṛkodaraḥ vasuṣeṇaṃ ca pāñcālaḥ kṛtsnena vyadhamad raṇe
english: The son of Kuntī crushed the saṃśaptakas, and Vṛkodara the Kurus, and the Pāñcāla scattered Vasuṣeṇa utterly in the fray.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca tvaramāṇaḥ punaḥ kṛṣṇaḥ pārtham abhyavadac chanaiḥ paśya kauravya rājānam apayātāṃś ca pāṇḍavān
english: Saṃjaya said: Kṛṣṇa, hastening, again spoke softly to Pārtha: "Behold, O Kauravya, the king, and the Pāṇḍavas withdrawing."

sanskrit: karṇaṃ paśya mahāraṅge jvalantam iva pāvakam asau bhīmo maheṣvāsaḥ saṃnivṛtto raṇaṃ prati
english: "Behold Karṇa in the great arena, blazing like fire; and yonder the dread mighty archer Bhīma has turned back to the battle."

sanskrit: tam ete 'nu nivartante dhṛṣṭadyumnapurogamāḥ pāñcālānāṃ sṛñjayānāṃ pāṇḍavānāṃ ca yan mukham nivṛttaiś ca tathā pārthair bhagnaṃ śatrubalaṃ mahat
english: "After him these turn back, led by Dhṛṣṭadyumna — the foremost of the Pāñcālas, the Sṛñjayas, and the Pāṇḍavas; and by the returning Pārthas the great host of the enemy is broken."

sanskrit: kauravān dravato hy eṣa karṇo dhārayate 'rjuna antakapratimo vege śakratulyaparākramaḥ
english: "This Karṇa, O Arjuna, stays the fleeing Kauravas — like Death himself in his onset, equal to Śakra in valor."

sanskrit: asau gacchati kauravya drauṇir astrabhṛtāṃ varaḥ tam eṣa pradrutaḥ saṃkhye dhṛṣṭadyumno mahārathaḥ
english: "Yonder goes Drauṇi, O Kauravya, the best of those who bear weapons; and Dhṛṣṭadyumna, the great chariot-warrior, rushes upon him in the fray."

sanskrit: sarvaṃ vyācaṣṭa durdharṣo vāsudevaḥ kirīṭine tato rājan prādurāsīn mahāghoro mahāraṇaḥ
english: All this the unassailable Vāsudeva recounted to the Diademed One; and thereupon, O king, a most terrible, mighty battle arose.

sanskrit: siṃhanādaravāś cātra prādurāsan samāgame ubhayoḥ senayo rājan mṛtyuṃ kṛtvā nivartanam
english: And lion-roars rang out there at the clash, O king, of both the armies — who had made of death their only turning-back.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca tataḥ punaḥ samājagmur abhītāḥ kurusṛñjayāḥ yudhiṣṭhiramukhāḥ pārthā vaikartanamukhā vayam
english: Saṃjaya said: Then the Kurus and the Sṛñjayas, unafraid, came together once more — the Pārthas with Yudhiṣṭhira at their head, and we with Vaikartana at ours.

sanskrit: tataḥ pravavṛte bhīmaḥ saṃgrāmo lomaharṣaṇaḥ karṇasya pāṇḍavānāṃ ca yamarāṣṭravivardhanaḥ
english: Then there began a fearful, hair-raising battle between Karṇa and the Pāṇḍavas, swelling the realm of Yama.

sanskrit: tasmin pravṛtte saṃgrāme tumule śoṇitodake saṃśaptakeṣu śūreṣu kiṃcicchiṣṭeṣu bhārata
english: When that tumultuous battle, whose waters were blood, had broken forth — the valiant saṃśaptakas being now but a remnant, O Bhārata —

sanskrit: dhṛṣṭadyumno mahārāja sahitaḥ sarvarājabhiḥ karṇam evābhidudrāva pāṇḍavāś ca mahārathāḥ
english: Dhṛṣṭadyumna, O great king, together with all the kings, and the Pāṇḍava great chariot-warriors, charged straight at Karṇa.

sanskrit: āgacchamānāṃs tān saṃkhye prahṛṣṭān vijayaiṣiṇaḥ dadhāraiko raṇe karṇo jalaughān iva parvataḥ
english: As they came on in the fray, exultant and eager for victory, Karṇa alone withstood them in the battle, as a mountain withstands floods of water.

sanskrit: tam āsādya tu te karṇaṃ vyaśīryanta mahārathāḥ yathācalaṃ samāsādya jalaughāḥ sarvatodiśam tayor āsīn mahārāja saṃgrāmo lomaharṣaṇaḥ
english: Reaching that Karṇa, those great chariot-warriors were scattered, as floods of water are scattered in all directions on meeting a mountain; and between the two, O great king, the battle was hair-raising.

sanskrit: dhṛṣṭadyumnas tu rādheyaṃ śareṇa nataparvaṇā tāḍayām āsa saṃkruddhas tiṣṭha tiṣṭheti cābravīt
english: But Dhṛṣṭadyumna, in his wrath, struck Rādheya with a smooth-jointed shaft and cried, "Stand! Stand!"

sanskrit: vijayaṃ tu dhanuḥśreṣṭhaṃ vidhunvāno mahārathaḥ pārṣatasya dhanuś chittvā śarān āśīviṣopamān tāḍayām āsa saṃkruddhaḥ pārṣataṃ navabhiḥ śaraiḥ
english: But the great chariot-warrior, brandishing Vijaya, his peerless bow, cut asunder the bow of Pārṣata and, full of wrath, smote the son of Pṛṣata with nine shafts like venomous serpents.

sanskrit: te varma hemavikṛtaṃ bhittvā tasya mahātmanaḥ śoṇitāktā vyarājanta śakragopā ivānagha
english: Those shafts, having pierced the gold-wrought armor of that great-souled one, gleamed smeared with blood like śakra-gopa beetles, O sinless one.

sanskrit: tad apāsya dhanuś chinnaṃ dhṛṣṭadyumno mahārathaḥ anyad dhanur upādāya śarāṃś cāśīviṣopamān karṇaṃ vivyādha saptatyā śaraiḥ saṃnataparvabhiḥ
english: Casting aside that severed bow, the great chariot-warrior Dhṛṣṭadyumna took up another bow, and with arrows like venomous serpents pierced Karṇa with seventy smooth-jointed shafts.

sanskrit: tathaiva rājan karṇo 'pi pārṣataṃ śatrutāpanam droṇaśatruṃ maheṣvāso vivyādha niśitaiḥ śaraiḥ
english: In like manner, O king, Karṇa too, that mighty archer, pierced with sharpened shafts the scorcher of foes, Pārṣata, the enemy of Droṇa.

sanskrit: tasya karṇo mahārāja śaraṃ kanakabhūṣaṇam preṣayām āsa saṃkruddho mṛtyudaṇḍam ivāparam
english: At him Karṇa, O great king, in his fury sped a gold-adorned shaft, like a second rod of Death.

sanskrit: tam āpatantaṃ sahasā ghorarūpaṃ viśāṃ pate ciccheda saptadhā rājañ śaineyaḥ kṛtahastavat
english: As it swiftly fell upon him, that shaft of dreadful form, O lord of peoples, the grandson of Śini, deft of hand, cut it sevenfold, O king.

sanskrit: dṛṣṭvā vinihitaṃ bāṇaṃ śaraiḥ karṇo viśāṃ pate sātyakiṃ śaravarṣeṇa samantāt paryavārayat
english: Seeing his arrow thus brought down by shafts, O lord of peoples, Karṇa enveloped Sātyaki on every side with a shower of arrows.

sanskrit: vivyādha cainaṃ samare nārācais tatra saptabhiḥ taṃ pratyavidhyac chaineyaḥ śarair hemavibhūṣitaiḥ
english: And he pierced him in that battle with seven iron shafts; the grandson of Śini in turn pierced him with arrows adorned with gold.

sanskrit: tato yuddham atīvāsīc cakṣuḥśrotrabhayāvaham rājan ghoraṃ ca citraṃ ca prekṣaṇīyaṃ samantataḥ
english: Then the combat grew exceedingly fierce, terrifying to eye and ear, O king — dreadful and wondrous, and on every side worth the beholding.

sanskrit: sarveṣāṃ tatra bhūtānāṃ lomaharṣo vyajāyata tad dṛṣṭvā samare karma karṇaśaineyayor nṛpa
english: In all the beings there a thrill of horror arose, beholding that feat in battle of Karṇa and the grandson of Śini, O king.

sanskrit: etasminn antare drauṇir abhyayāt sumahābalam pārṣataṃ śatrudamanaṃ śatruvīryāsunāśanam
english: In this interval Drauṇi advanced against the exceedingly mighty Pārṣata, tamer of foes, destroyer of the valor and the lives of enemies.

sanskrit: abhyabhāṣata saṃkruddho drauṇir dūre dhanaṃjaye tiṣṭha tiṣṭhādya brahmaghna na me jīvan vimokṣyase
english: Dhanaṃjaya being far off, Drauṇi spoke in his wrath: "Stand! Stand this day, slayer of a Brāhmaṇa — you shall not escape me alive!"

sanskrit: ity uktvā subhṛśaṃ vīraḥ śīghrakṛn niśitaiḥ śaraiḥ pārṣataṃ chādayām āsa ghorarūpaiḥ sutejanaiḥ yatamānaṃ paraṃ śaktyā yatamāno mahārathaḥ
english: So saying, the swift-handed hero, that great chariot-warrior, straining to his utmost might, overwhelmed with sharp, keen-edged, dreadful shafts the Pārṣata, who likewise strove with all his power.

sanskrit: yathā hi samare drauṇiḥ pārṣataṃ vīkṣya māriṣa tathā drauṇiṃ raṇe dṛṣṭvā pārṣataḥ paravīrahā nātihṛṣṭamanā bhūtvā manyate mṛtyum ātmanaḥ
english: For as Drauṇi, beholding Pārṣata in battle, O honored one, so too the Pārṣata, slayer of hostile heroes, beholding Drauṇi in the fray, grew not greatly glad of heart, but deemed his own death at hand.

sanskrit: drauṇis tu dṛṣṭvā rājendra dhṛṣṭadyumnaṃ raṇe sthitam krodhena niḥśvasan vīraḥ pārṣataṃ samupādravat tāv anyonyaṃ tu dṛṣṭvaiva saṃrambhaṃ jagmatuḥ param
english: But Drauṇi, O lord of kings, seeing Dhṛṣṭadyumna standing firm in the fray, hissing with rage, the hero rushed upon the Pārṣata; and at the mere sight of each other the two were seized with utmost fury.

sanskrit: athābravīn mahārāja droṇaputraḥ pratāpavān dhṛṣṭadyumnaṃ samīpasthaṃ tvaramāṇo viśāṃ pate pāñcālāpasadādya tvāṃ preṣayiṣyāmi mṛtyave
english: Then the valiant son of Droṇa, O great king, said in haste to Dhṛṣṭadyumna who stood near, O lord of peoples: "Basest of the Pāñcālas, this day I shall send you to your death!"

sanskrit: pāpaṃ hi yat tvayā karma ghnatā droṇaṃ purā kṛtam adya tvā patsyate tad vai yathā hy akuśalaṃ tathā
english: "The sinful deed you wrought of old in slaying Droṇa shall this day fall back upon you, as surely as ill-doing brings its fruit."

sanskrit: arakṣyamāṇaḥ pārthena yadi tiṣṭhasi saṃyuge nāpakramasi vā mūḍha satyam etad bravīmi te
english: "If, unguarded by Pārtha, you stand your ground in the fight, and do not flee, O fool — this truth I tell you."

sanskrit: evam uktaḥ pratyuvāca dhṛṣṭadyumnaḥ pratāpavān prativākyaṃ sa evāsir māmako dāsyate tava yenaiva te pitur dattaṃ yatamānasya saṃyuge
english: Thus addressed, the valiant Dhṛṣṭadyumna answered in reply: "That same sword of mine shall give you what it gave your father as he strove in the fight."

sanskrit: yadi tāvan mayā droṇo nihato brāhmaṇabruvaḥ tvām idānīṃ kathaṃ yuddhe na haniṣyāmi vikramāt
english: "If indeed Droṇa, that so-called Brāhmaṇa, was slain by me, how then shall I not now slay you in battle by my valor?"

sanskrit: evam uktvā mahārāja senāpatir amarṣaṇaḥ niśitenātha bāṇena drauṇiṃ vivyādha pārṣataḥ
english: So saying, O great king, the wrathful commander, the Pārṣata, pierced Drauṇi with a sharpened arrow.

sanskrit: tato drauṇiḥ susaṃkruddhaḥ śaraiḥ saṃnataparvabhiḥ prācchādayad diśo rājan dhṛṣṭadyumnasya saṃyuge
english: Then Drauṇi, exceedingly enraged, with smooth-jointed shafts veiled all the quarters about Dhṛṣṭadyumna in the fight, O king.

sanskrit: naivāntarikṣaṃ na diśo naiva yodhāḥ samantataḥ dṛśyante vai mahārāja śaraiś channāḥ sahasraśaḥ
english: Neither the sky, nor the quarters, nor the warriors round about could be seen, O great king, so veiled were they by arrows in their thousands.

sanskrit: tathaiva pārṣato rājan drauṇim āhavaśobhinam śaraiḥ saṃchādayām āsa sūtaputrasya paśyataḥ
english: In like manner the Pārṣata, O king, veiled with arrows Drauṇi, who shone in the fray, even as the son of the sūta looked on.

sanskrit: rādheyo 'pi mahārāja pāñcālān saha pāṇḍavaiḥ draupadeyān yudhāmanyuṃ sātyakiṃ ca mahāratham ekaḥ sa vārayām āsa prekṣaṇīyaḥ samantataḥ
english: Rādheya too, O great king, alone held in check the Pāñcālas together with the Pāṇḍavas, the sons of Draupadī, Yudhāmanyu, and the great chariot-warrior Sātyaki — a sight to behold on every side.

sanskrit: dhṛṣṭadyumno 'pi samare drauṇeś ciccheda kārmukam tad apāsya dhanuś chinnam anyad ādatta kārmukam vegavat samare ghoraṃ śarāṃś cāśīviṣopamān
english: Dhṛṣṭadyumna too in the fray cut asunder Drauṇi's bow; casting aside that severed bow, Drauṇi took up another, swift and dreadful in battle, with arrows like venomous serpents.

sanskrit: sa pārṣatasya rājendra dhanuḥ śaktiṃ gadāṃ dhvajam hayān sūtaṃ rathaṃ caiva nimeṣād vyadhamac charaiḥ
english: He, O lord of kings, in the twinkling of an eye shattered with his shafts the Pārṣata's bow, his lance, his mace, his banner, his horses, his charioteer, and his chariot itself.

sanskrit: sa chinnadhanvā viratho hatāśvo hatasārathiḥ khaḍgam ādatta vipulaṃ śatacandraṃ ca bhānumat
english: He, his bow cut, his chariot lost, his horses slain, his charioteer slain, took up a broad sword and a hundred-mooned shield, gleaming bright.

sanskrit: drauṇis tad api rājendra bhallaiḥ kṣipraṃ mahārathaḥ ciccheda samare vīraḥ kṣiprahasto dṛḍhāyudhaḥ rathād anavarūḍhasya tad adbhutam ivābhavat
english: But Drauṇi too, O lord of kings, that great chariot-warrior, swift of hand and firm in arms, the hero swiftly cut these asunder in the fray with broad-headed shafts — and that, while he had not stepped down from his chariot, seemed a marvel.

sanskrit: dhṛṣṭadyumnaṃ tu virathaṃ hatāśvaṃ chinnakārmukam śaraiś ca bahudhā viddham astraiś ca śakalīkṛtam nātarad bharataśreṣṭha yatamāno mahārathaḥ
english: Yet Dhṛṣṭadyumna — chariotless, his horses slain, his bow cut, pierced again and again by shafts and hewn to pieces by weapons — that great chariot-warrior, for all his striving, the foremost of the Bhāratas could not overcome.

sanskrit: tasyāntam iṣubhī rājan yadā drauṇir na jagmivān atha tyaktvā dhanur vīraḥ pārṣataṃ tvarito 'nvagāt
english: When Drauṇi could not make an end of him with his arrows, O king, then the hero, casting aside his bow, hastily pursued the Pārṣata.

sanskrit: āsīd ādravato rājan vegas tasya mahātmanaḥ garuḍasyeva patato jighṛkṣoḥ pannagottamam
english: The onset of that great-souled one as he rushed forth, O king, was like that of Garuḍa swooping down, eager to seize the foremost of serpents.

sanskrit: etasminn eva kāle tu mādhavo 'rjunam abravīt paśya pārtha yathā drauṇiḥ pārṣatasya vadhaṃ prati yatnaṃ karoti vipulaṃ hanyāc cainam asaṃśayam
english: At that very moment Mādhava said to Arjuna: "Behold, O Pārtha, how Drauṇi makes mighty effort to slay the Pārṣata — without doubt he will slay him."

sanskrit: taṃ mocaya mahābāho pārṣataṃ śatrutāpanam drauṇer āsyam anuprāptaṃ mṛtyor āsyagataṃ yathā
english: "Deliver him, O mighty-armed — the Pārṣata, scorcher of foes, who has come into the jaws of Drauṇi as one fallen into the jaws of Death."

sanskrit: evam uktvā mahārāja vāsudevaḥ pratāpavān praiṣayat tatra turagān yatra drauṇir vyavasthitaḥ
english: So saying, O great king, the valiant Vāsudeva sped the horses thither, to where Drauṇi was stationed.

sanskrit: te hayāś candrasaṃkāśāḥ keśavena pracoditāḥ pibanta iva tad vyoma jagmur drauṇirathaṃ prati
english: Those horses, bright as the moon, urged on by Keśava, sped toward Drauṇi's chariot as though drinking up the sky.

sanskrit: dṛṣṭvāyāntau mahāvīryāv ubhau kṛṣṇadhanaṃjayau dhṛṣṭadyumnavadhe rājaṃś cakre yatnaṃ mahābalaḥ
english: Seeing the two of mighty valor, Kṛṣṇa and Dhanaṃjaya, coming on, the strong one, O king, redoubled his effort to slay Dhṛṣṭadyumna.

sanskrit: vikṛṣyamāṇaṃ dṛṣṭvaiva dhṛṣṭadyumnaṃ janeśvara śarāṃś cikṣepa vai pārtho drauṇiṃ prati mahābalaḥ
english: At the mere sight of Dhṛṣṭadyumna being dragged off, O lord of men, the mighty Pārtha hurled his shafts against Drauṇi.

sanskrit: te śarā hemavikṛtā gāṇḍīvapreṣitā bhṛśam drauṇim āsādya viviśur valmīkam iva pannagāḥ
english: Those gold-wrought arrows, sped forcefully from the Gāṇḍīva, reaching Drauṇi entered him as serpents enter an anthill.

sanskrit: sa vidhvastaiḥ śarair ghorair droṇaputraḥ pratāpavān ratham āruruhe vīro dhanaṃjayaśarārditaḥ pragṛhya ca dhanuḥ śreṣṭhaṃ pārthaṃ vivyādha sāyakaiḥ
english: Scattered by those dreadful shafts, the valiant son of Droṇa, tormented by the arrows of Dhanaṃjaya, the hero mounted his chariot, and seizing his peerless bow pierced Pārtha with his darts.

sanskrit: etasminn antare vīraḥ sahadevo janādhipa apovāha rathenājau pārṣataṃ śatrutāpanam
english: In this interval the hero Sahadeva, O ruler of men, bore the Pārṣata, scorcher of foes, away from the fray upon his chariot.

sanskrit: arjuno 'pi mahārāja drauṇiṃ vivyādha patribhiḥ taṃ droṇaputraḥ saṃkruddho bāhvor urasi cārdayat
english: Arjuna too, O great king, pierced Drauṇi with feathered shafts; and the son of Droṇa, enraged, smote him upon the arms and the breast.

sanskrit: krodhitas tu raṇe pārtho nārācaṃ kālasaṃmitam droṇaputrāya cikṣepa kāladaṇḍam ivāparam sa brāhmaṇasyāṃsadeśe nipapāta mahādyutiḥ
english: But Pārtha, enraged in battle, hurled at the son of Droṇa an iron shaft, the measure of Doom, like a second rod of Time; and it, of great splendor, fell upon the Brāhmaṇa's shoulder.

sanskrit: sa vihvalo mahārāja śaravegena saṃyuge niṣasāda rathopasthe vaiklavyaṃ ca paraṃ yayau
english: Reeling, O great king, from the force of that shaft in the fight, he sank down upon the floor of his chariot and fell into utter distress.

sanskrit: tataḥ karṇo mahārāja vyākṣipad vijayaṃ dhanuḥ arjunaṃ samare kruddhaḥ prekṣamāṇo muhur muhuḥ dvairathaṃ cāpi pārthena kāmayāno mahāraṇe
english: Then Karṇa, O great king, drew the bow named Vijaya, gazing again and again in wrath upon Arjuna in the fray, longing for single combat with Pārtha in that great battle.

sanskrit: taṃ tu hitvā hataṃ vīraṃ sārathiḥ śatrukarśanam apovāha rathenājau tvaramāṇo raṇājirāt
english: But the charioteer, leaving aside that stricken hero, harrier of foes, bore him in haste away from the field of battle upon his chariot.

sanskrit: athotkruṣṭaṃ mahārāja pāñcālair jitakāśibhiḥ mokṣitaṃ pārṣataṃ dṛṣṭvā droṇaputraṃ ca pīḍitam
english: Then a great shout went up, O great king, from the Pāñcālas flushed with victory, beholding the Pārṣata delivered and the son of Droṇa hard pressed.

sanskrit: vāditrāṇi ca divyāni prāvādyanta sahasraśaḥ siṃhanādaś ca saṃjajñe dṛṣṭvā ghoraṃ mahādbhutam
english: And divine instruments sounded forth by the thousands, and a lion-roar arose at the sight of that dreadful, great marvel.

sanskrit: evaṃ kṛtvābravīt pārtho vāsudevaṃ dhanaṃjayaḥ yāhi saṃśaptakān kṛṣṇa kāryam etat paraṃ mama
english: Having done thus, Pārtha Dhanaṃjaya said to Vāsudeva: "Drive on to the saṃśaptakas, O Kṛṣṇa — this is my supreme task."

sanskrit: tataḥ prayāto dāśārhaḥ śrutvā pāṇḍavabhāṣitam rathenātipatākena manomārutaraṃhasā
english: Then the Dāśārha, hearing the Pāṇḍava's word, drove onward in his richly bannered chariot, swift as the mind and the wind.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca etasminn antare kṛṣṇaḥ pārthaṃ vacanam abravīt darśayann iva kaunteyaṃ dharmarājaṃ yudhiṣṭhiram
english: Saṃjaya said: In this interval Kṛṣṇa spoke a word to Pārtha, as though pointing out to the son of Kuntī the Dharma-king Yudhiṣṭhira.

sanskrit: eṣa pāṇḍava te bhrātā dhārtarāṣṭrair mahābalaiḥ jighāṃsubhir maheṣvāsair drutaṃ pārthānusaryate
english: "Yonder, O Pāṇḍava, your brother is swiftly pursued by the mighty sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, great archers bent on his slaying, O Pārtha."

sanskrit: tathānuyānti saṃrabdhāḥ pāñcālā yuddhadurmadāḥ yudhiṣṭhiraṃ mahātmānaṃ parīpsanto mahājavāḥ
english: "And the Pāñcālas, enraged and frenzied in battle, follow after at great speed, seeking to save the great-souled Yudhiṣṭhira."

sanskrit: eṣa duryodhanaḥ pārtha rathānīkena daṃśitaḥ rājā sarvasya lokasya rājānam anudhāvati
english: "Yonder Duryodhana, O Pārtha, mailed and ringed by his host of chariots — that king of all the world — runs in pursuit of the king."

sanskrit: jighāṃsuḥ puruṣavyāghraṃ bhrātṛbhiḥ sahito balī āśīviṣasamasparśaiḥ sarvayuddhaviśāradaiḥ
english: "Eager to slay that tiger among men, the mighty one, together with his brothers — whose touch is like a venomous serpent's, skilled in every mode of war."

sanskrit: ete jighṛkṣavo yānti dvipāśvarathapattayaḥ yudhiṣṭhiraṃ dhārtarāṣṭrā ratnottamam ivārthinaḥ
english: "These sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra advance with their elephants, horses, chariots, and foot, eager to seize Yudhiṣṭhira as suitors covet a most precious jewel."

sanskrit: paśya sātvatabhīmābhyāṃ niruddhādhiṣṭhitaḥ prabhuḥ jihīrṣavo 'mṛtaṃ daityāḥ śakrāgnibhyām ivāvaśāḥ
english: "Behold — the lord, hemmed in and guarded by the Sātvata and by Bhīma, as the Daityas, eager to carry off the nectar, were held helpless by Śakra and Agni."

sanskrit: ete bahutvāt tvaritāḥ punar gacchanti pāṇḍavam samudram iva vāryoghāḥ prāvṛṭkāle mahārathāḥ
english: "By force of their numbers these great chariot-warriors, hastening, advance again upon the Pāṇḍava, as floods of water flow to the sea in the rainy season."

sanskrit: nadantaḥ siṃhanādāṃś ca dhamantaś cāpi vārijān balavanto maheṣvāsā vidhunvanto dhanūṃṣi ca
english: "Roaring with lion-roars, blowing too their conch-shells, those strong mighty archers, brandishing their bows withal —"

sanskrit: mṛtyor mukhagataṃ manye kuntīputraṃ yudhiṣṭhiram hutam agnau ca bhadraṃ te duryodhanavaśaṃ gatam
english: "I deem the son of Kuntī, Yudhiṣṭhira, fallen into the jaws of Death, offered up into the fire — blessings on you — gone into Duryodhana's power."

sanskrit: yathāyuktam anīkaṃ hi dhārtarāṣṭrasya pāṇḍava nāsya śakro 'pi mucyeta saṃprāpto bāṇagocaram
english: "For so well arrayed is the host of Dhṛtarāṣṭra's son, O Pāṇḍava, that not even Śakra, once come within range of its arrows, could win free of it."

sanskrit: duryodhanasya śūrasya drauṇeḥ śāradvatasya ca karṇasya ceṣuvego vai parvatān api dārayet
english: "The arrow-force of the valiant Duryodhana, of Drauṇi, of the son of Śaradvat, and of Karṇa, could rend asunder even the mountains."
